Multi-Cue Normal-Inverse-Chi-Squared (MNIX) Family: Representations, Templates, and Models

Source: R/S7-class-mnix.R
family-mnix.Rd

Constructs and manages multi-cue Normal-Inverse-\(\chi^2\) (MNIX) category representations, templates, and ideal adaptors under early and late cue integration.

Usage

new_mnix_category_representation(
  category_labels,
  cue_labels,
  m,
  kappa,
  nu,
  sigma2,
  weights = NULL,
  metadata = list()
)

new_mnix_category_representation_from_data(
  data,
  category = "category",
  cues,
  kappa = nu,
  nu = 3,
  ...
)

new_mnix_category_representation_template_from_data(
  data,
  category = "category",
  cues,
  kappa = nu,
  nu = 3,
  ...
)

new_mnix_ideal_adaptor_ideal_integrator(
  category_template = NULL,
  decision_rule = "sampling",
  category_prior = NULL,
  lapse_rate = 0,
  lapse_bias = NULL,
  Sigma_noise = NULL,
  noise_treatment = .infer_noise_treatment(Sigma_noise),
  lapse_treatment = .infer_lapse_treatment(lapse_rate),
  metadata = list()
)

new_mnix_ideal_adaptor_category_adaptive_weighted_integrator(...)

Arguments

metadata

Optional list of metadata. Defaults to list().

m

Numeric vector of per-cue location hyperparameters.

kappa

Positive numeric scalar or vector of precision scalings (\(\kappa > 0\)). For late integration, a vector of length equal to cues (or scalar recycled across cues). For early integration, a scalar reflecting composite dimension belief strength.

nu

Positive numeric scalar or vector of degrees of freedom (\(\nu > 2\)). For late integration, a vector of length equal to cues (or scalar recycled across cues). For early integration, a scalar reflecting composite dimension degrees of freedom.

sigma2

Numeric vector of per-cue scale parameters.

weights

Numeric vector or matrix of integration/attention weights. For representations and global weighted models, a numeric simplex vector summing to 1. For category-weighted models, an \(M \times K\) matrix whose rows each sum to 1.

category_labels

Character vector of category label(s).

cue_labels

Character vector of cue labels (at least 2 cue dimensions).

data

Data frame containing category and cue observations.

category

Character string indicating the category column in data. Defaults to "category".

cues

Character vector indicating cue columns in data (at least 2 cues).

...

Additional arguments passed to methods or constructors.

category_template

An MVBU_CategoryRepresentationTemplate object containing MNIX category representations.

decision_rule

Categorization decision rule: "sampling", "criterion", or "proportional". Defaults to "sampling".

category_prior

Optional numeric vector of prior category probabilities summing to 1. Defaults to equal priors.

lapse_rate

Numeric scalar lapse probability in [0, 1]. Defaults to 0.

lapse_bias

Optional numeric vector of lapse category probabilities summing to 1. Defaults to uniform bias 1/M.

Sigma_noise

Optional perceptual/measurement noise covariance matrix or vector.

noise_treatment

Treatment of perceptual noise during evaluation and updating: "no_noise", "sample", or "marginalize".

  • "no_noise": No perceptual noise is applied to input cues, and no noise is assumed during categorization.

  • "sample": Simulates sensory noise on a specific observation. Noise drawn from \(\mathcal{N}(0, \Sigma_{\text{noise}})\) is added to input cues (and projected into composite cue space in early integration), and the observer accounts for their own noise uncertainty during categorization by adding \(\Sigma_{\text{noise}}\) to their likelihood scale.

  • "marginalize": Evaluates categorization in the limit across infinitely many noisy encounters (expected consequences). No noise is sampled onto the input stimulus, but \(\Sigma_{\text{noise}}\) is added to the category covariance scale.

Defaults to .infer_noise_treatment(Sigma_noise): "marginalize" if noise is present, "no_noise" otherwise.

lapse_treatment

Treatment of attentional lapses during evaluation and updating: "no_lapses", "sample", or "marginalize".

  • "no_lapses": Lapses are ignored; categorization and updating reflect pure normative evidence evaluation (even if lapse_rate > 0).

  • "sample": Simulates stochastic attentional lapses on individual observations. With probability lapse_rate, a lapse occurs: during categorization, the posterior is replaced by lapse_bias; during updating, the lapsing observation is treated as uninformative.

  • "marginalize": Evaluates categorization in the limit across infinitely many encounters (expected response probabilities). The category posterior is the mixture \((1 - \lambda) p(c \mid x) + \lambda b_c\), and evidence during updating is downweighted by \(1 - \lambda\).

Defaults to .infer_lapse_treatment(lapse_rate): "marginalize" if lapse_rate > 0, "no_lapses" otherwise.

weights_matrix

Deprecated. Use weights instead.

input_cues

Deprecated. Use cues instead.

Value

An S7 object of the respective MNIX class.

Details

The MNIX family unifies multi-cue belief updating under both late and early integration regimes:

  • Late Integration: Categories are represented by independent marginal Student-\(t\) predictive components along each cue dimension (\(\kappa\) and \(\nu\) have length \(K\)). Cue log-likelihoods are combined at decision time via Bayes rule or attention weights.

  • Early Integration: Multi-cue observations are projected to a composite dimension \(z = \mathbf{w}^\top \mathbf{x}\) prior to updating (\(\kappa\) and \(\nu\) are scalar length 1).

See also

family-muvg, family-niw, family-nix

Examples

# Mixture / Multivariate NIX representation
mu_b <- c(VOT = 10, f0 = 200)
sigma2_b <- c(VOT = 25, f0 = 36)
rep_b <- new_mnix_category_representation(
  category_labels = "/b/", cue_labels = c("VOT", "f0"),
  m = mu_b, kappa = c(5, 5), nu = c(8, 8),
  sigma2 = sigma2_b
)
mu_d <- c(VOT = 50, f0 = 240)
sigma2_d <- c(VOT = 25, f0 = 36)
rep_d <- new_mnix_category_representation(
  category_labels = "/d/", cue_labels = c("VOT", "f0"),
  m = mu_d, kappa = c(5, 5), nu = c(8, 8),
  sigma2 = sigma2_d
)
tmpl <- new_category_representation_template(list(rep_b, rep_d))
m_mnix <- new_mnix_ideal_adaptor(category_template = tmpl)
m_mnix
#> <MVBeliefUpdatr::MNIX_IdealAdaptor_IdealIntegrator>
#>   Categories (2): /b/, /d/
#>   Cues (2): VOT, f0
#>   Decision rule: sampling
#>   Category prior: /b/: 0.5, /d/: 0.5
#>   Lapse rate: 0 (treatment: no_lapses)
#>   Perceptual noise: none (treatment: no_noise)
#>   Category representations (2):
#>     /b/: MNIX(kappa = vector(2), nu = vector(2), m = vector(2), sigma2 = vector(2))
#>       E[mu] = vector(2), E[Sigma] = matrix(2, 2), Sigma_marg = matrix(2, 2)
#>     /d/: MNIX(kappa = vector(2), nu = vector(2), m = vector(2), sigma2 = vector(2))
#>       E[mu] = vector(2), E[Sigma] = matrix(2, 2), Sigma_marg = matrix(2, 2)
